prerequisites: Physics in 2nd year of high school
prior mathematical knowledge of vector calculus, trigonometry, and differentiation and integration of single-variable functions

learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge of basic and technological subjects, which enable the student to learn new methods and technologies, as well as providing them with great versatility to adapt to new situations.

Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills and abilities, understanding the ethical and professional responsibility of their activity.
Ability to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills and abilities in the corresponding field of Engineering, both orally and in writing, and to all types of audiences.
Honesty, responsibility, ethical commitment and spirit of solidarity.
Ability to work in a team.
Understanding and mastery of the basic concepts about the general laws of waves and electromagnetism and their application for solving problems typical of engineering.
Understand the concept of a wave and know its mathematical characterization as well as basic wave phenomena.
Know the basic concepts and laws of electromagnetism and apply them to the analysis of simple electromagnetic situations in vacuum and in material media.
Correctly handle the recommended physical symbology, both in terms of magnitudes and units.
Learn and put into practice problem-solving strategies related to the different contents of the course.
Acquire skills related to laboratory work and to the treatment of measurements and errors.

syllabus_topics: Corriente eléctrica: Intensidad y densidad de corriente eléctrica
Fuerza magnética sobre una corriente eléctrica
Momento del campo magnético sobre una espira
Campos electromagnéticos variables con el tiempo: Inducción electromagnética: Ley de Faraday-Henry
Ondas: Generalidades. Ondas mecánicas: Concepto de onda
Práctica 1. Ley de Ohm / Circuitos de Corriente Continua
Práctica 2. Carga del Condensador / Campo Magnético de un Solenoide
Práctica 4. Ondas Mecánicas / Ondas Estacionarias en una Cuerda
teaching_methods: Expository classes (lectures and explanations of theoretical content, exemplification and problem solving)
Classroom practices/seminars (problem solving, group work, presentation and defense of problems/projects)
Laboratory practices (handling lab equipment, use of simulation/data processing software, analysis of results and report writing)
Problem solving and preparation of practice reports, assignments

assessment_methods.method: Partial Exam (T2) on theoretical content (excluding T1)
Theoretical Exam (ET) on all theoretical content

assessment_rules: For the ordinary call, if minimums for Partial Exams T1 and T2 are met (T1>=5/10, T2>=4/10), the theory grade is (0.35 x T1) + (0.40 x T2) + (0.10 x PA). If the T1 minimum is not met, the theory grade is (0.75 x ET) + (0.10 x PA), where ET requires a minimum of 4/10. For practicals, 75% attendance is mandatory. If minimums for the practical block are met, the practical grade is (0.08 x P1) + (0.07 x P2). The final grade is (Theory) + (Practicals) if all minimums are reached and attendance is met; otherwise, the final grade is the minimum of the calculated score and 4.0. For the extraordinary call, the theory grade is (0.75 x ET) + (0.10 x PA), with ET requiring a minimum of 4/10. The practical grade (P1) is maintained if attendance was >= 75%; if attendance was < 75%, a Practical Exam (P2) is taken with a minimum of 4/10, and the practical grade is (0.15 x P2).
